questions.q: The theory that can completely/properly explain the nature of bonding in  \left[Ni \left(CO\right)4\right]$ is:$
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
There is synergic bonding present in& \left[Ni \left(CO\right)4\right]$.

As~$CO$~is neutral ligand, so oxidation state of nickel is zero i.e.${Ni}^{0}$.

So, electronic configuration of~${Ni}^{0}$~$= \left[Ar\right]3d^{8}4s^{2}$

As~$CO$~is strong field ligand, it will back paired the 4s electrons to $3d$ orbitals.

So in complex electronic configuration of~${Ni}^{0}$~$= \left[Ar\right]3d^{10}4s^{0}$~here inner d orbital is filled.

In ligand~$CO$~(carbonyl) the anti-bonding orbital is vacant.

$CO: \sigma1s^{2}, \sigma* 1s^{2}, \sigma2s^{2}, \sigma* 2s^{2}, \sigma2{p}_z^{2}, {πp}_x^{2} = {πp}_y^{2}, \pi* {p}_x^{0} = \pi* {p}_y^{0}$

The fully filled inner d-orbital of central metal atom gives it's electrons to vacant~$\pi$~anti-bonding orbital, this is called back~$\pi$~bonding, due to this back bonding bond between metal and ligand is very strong.

This back~$\pi$~bonding is also called synergic bonding and this synergic bonding is explained by molecular orbital theory.

Carbon monoxide~$CO$ made synergic bonding with Haemoglobin& in are blood, as synergic bonding is very strong, so oxygen taking capacity of haemoglobin decrease and it cause death.

$

questions.q:
The correct statements among I to III are:
(I) Valence bond theory cannot explain the color exhibited by transition metal complexes.
(II) Valence bond theory can predict quantitatively the magnetic properties of transition metal complexes.
(III) Valence bond theory cannot distinguish ligands as weak and strong field ones.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Valence Bond Theory (VBT) has several limitations in explaining the properties of coordination compounds.

Statement (I) is correct. VBT does not explain the optical properties or the color exhibited by transition metal complexes. The color is primarily due to d-d electron transitions, which are successfully explained by Crystal Field Theory (CFT).

Statement (II) is incorrect. VBT only provides a qualitative idea about the magnetic properties, such as whether a complex is paramagnetic or diamagnetic based on the presence of unpaired electrons. It cannot predict magnetic properties quantitatively.

Statement (III) is correct. VBT does not distinguish between weak field and strong field ligands. It relies on experimentally observed magnetic moments to assume whether inner or outer d-orbitals are used for hybridization, without explaining why certain ligands cause electron pairing while others do not. The classification of ligands into weak and strong fields is a feature of CFT.

Therefore, only statements (I) and (III) are correct.

questions.q:
If ${Ni}^{2 +}$ is replaced by ${Pt}^{2 +}$ in the complex \left[{NiCl}_{2}{Br}_{2}\right]2 -$, which of the following properties are expected to get changed?
A. Geometry
B. Geometrical isomerism
C. Optical isomerism
D. Magnetic properties$
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
When${Ni}^{2 +}$ is replaced by${Pt}^{2 +}$ in the complex \left[{NiCl}_{2}{Br}_{2}\right]2 -$, the following properties are expected to be changed:

A. Geometry:~Since ${Pt}^{2 +}$ and${Ni}^{2 +}$ have different coordination preferences and atomic sizes, the replacement is likely to result in a change in the geometry of the complex. That is it changes to square planar.

B. Geometrical isomerism:~If the replacement of ${Ni}^{2 +}$ with ${Pt}^{2 +}$ leads to a change in the ligand arrangement, it can result in the generation of cis and trans isomers.

C. Magnetic properties:~\left[{PtCl}_{2}{Br}_{2}\right]2 -$& is diamagnetic.

Both the complex species are optically inactive.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
In \left[Ni\left({H}_{2}O\right)6\right]2 +$, ${H}_{2}O$ is a weak field ligand. Therefore, there are unpaired electrons in ${Ni}^{2 +}$. questions.q:
If the CFSE of \left[Ti\left({H}_{2}O\right)6\right]3 +$ is $- 96 . 0kJ / mol$, this complex will absorb maximum at wavelength $nm$. (nearest integer)

Assume Planck' constant $( h ) = 6 . 4 \times {10}^{- 34}Js$, Speed of light $( c ) = 3 . 0 \times {10}^{8}m / s$ and Avogadro's constant \left({N}_{A}\right) = 6 \times {10}^{23} / mol$.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
In& \left[Ti\left({H}_{2}O\right)6\right]3 +$, oxidation state of Titanium is +3.
Thus, electronic configuration:

${Ti}^{+ 3}: 3d^{1} ⇒ {t}_{2g}^{1, 0, 0}, {eg}^{0, 0}$

We know~CFSE~$= \left[- 0 . 4{n}_{t2g} + 0 . 6{n}_{eg}\right]\Delta o$~ ~ ~ ~(~ ~ $\Delta o = Octahedralsplittingenergy$)

$\Delta o = \dfrac{96 \times {10}^{3}}{0 . 4 \times 6 \times {10}^{23}} = 4 \times {10}^{- 19}J$

Using planck's equation and fact that octahedral splitting energy per complex is:
$⇒ \Delta o = \dfrac{hc}{λ} = 4 \times {10}^{- 19}J$

$⇒ \lambda = \dfrac{6 . 4 \times {10}^{- 34} \times 3 \times {10}^{8}}{4 \times {10}^{- 19}} = 4 . 8 \times {10}^{- 7}m$

$⇒ \lambda = 480 \times {10}^{- 9}m$

$∴ \lambda = 480nm$

$
